no-halpin-scandal-story.summary: In this world, the voters I interviewed lean 15.3 points further toward Cleveland than the same people did in 1884 as it was. California, Colorado, Iowa, Illinois and 13 more flip, but Cleveland still wins, 392–9. The closest call is Kansas, which holds for Blaine by 5.0 points. Blaine wins in 6 of 100 draws. Extremely low confidence. Historical evidence is thin: loose analogies or weak sources only.

howIGotThis: What changed: The Buffalo Evening Telegraph never publishes its July 1884 story that the Democratic nominee fathered a child out of wedlock with Maria Halpin, so the scandal and the 'Ma, Ma, where's my Pa?' taunts never enter the campaign.

What historians found (12 findings, weak evidence): No source measures the Halpin scandal's effect on any group or region. Secondary accounts disagree. HarpWeek says the prompt admission helped Cleveland's image of good character. HISTORY.com and a student article say the scandal hurt him and tightened New York. One older biography judges that only the July timing saved him. Mugwumps stayed with Cleveland, and the clergy were split. Cleveland carried New York by 1,047 votes, with Burchard also cited as decisive. The 1828 Jackson analogue gives no measurable scandal effect.
The numbers: the 1880 and 1890 census counts interpolated to 1884 and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1884 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

Extremely low confidence: Historical evidence is thin: loose analogies or weak sources only. 10 of 18 people interviewed took the news to be about the other candidate; their answers were left out. 19 groups the change reaches weren't interviewed; they borrow the interviewed groups' effect, with extra uncertainty.

Boston, Sept. 21. The Independent the administration party filled Tremont Temple last evening. reading.summary: Brief news: a planned work project, Wall Street stocks, and falling imports.
Prohibition candidate pledges to carry the standard; notification committee members are listed.
Writer says Kansas prohibition alternates between lawless drinking and violent crusades against it.
Maine's constitutional prohibition amendment wins triumphantly after thirty years of statutory prohibition.
Speakers debate whether prohibition works, citing letters from Mississippi officials praising its effects.

Humorous mosquito item, followed by a note on how France controls monopolies.
San Antonio report on a colored voters' convention held in a saloon hall.
Lecturer Gambrel says dry Mississippi counties see fewer court cases and more spending.
Supreme Court rules West Point cadet time counts toward longevity pay.
Mint report: gold and silver deposits and purchases total about $87.9 million.
Fulsome tribute praises a leader as defender of protection, unharmed by months of slander.
